extracted.intended_audience: sources (founders, spokespeople, PR/new practitioners) using HARO/Connectively to pitch reporters
extracted.subtask_description: Craft short, reporter-focused pitches in response to HARO (Connectively) queries: match the query, immediately establish relevant expertise, give a brief quotable answer with supporting data, and provide contact/headshot for rapid follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match query exactly (subject line)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line: match the query exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the query's subject in your email subject line verbatim (e.g., 'Subject: [Match exact query subject line]'). This helps reporters filter and immediately see relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify yourself and credentials immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: First line should identify who you are and your credentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with 'I'm [Name], [Title] at [Company]' and one credential relevant to the query so the reporter can immediately judge authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct, quotable answer to the question
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead with a concise direct answer — preferably 1–2 quotable sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters scan for usable quotes; provide a 1–2 sentence direct answer early (the transcript suggests a '2-sentence direct answer — quotable'). Make the phrasing stand-alone and clear so it can be lifted into copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use quotable phrasing (avoid stock closers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write sentences that are easy to quote and avoid non-quotable phrasing like 'in conclusion'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose crisp, declarative language reporters can quote. Avoid filler/formulaic signoffs and hedging that reduces quotability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay under 100 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the pitch short — pitches over 100 words are rarely used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brevity matters because reporters scan many responses; shorter pitches are more likely to be read and quoted directly. Aim to present your credentials and a 1–2 sentence quote plus brief supporting data within ~100 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide 1–2 specific examples or data points
rubrics_metrics.description: Include one or two concrete examples or data points to support your answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the direct answer, add brief, specific evidence (numbers, short anecdotes, or concrete examples) that make the quote actionable and verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include verifiable credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: List credentials relevant to the query that can be verified by the reporter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention titles, affiliations, degrees, published work, or other verifiable facts. Avoid vague or unverifiable claims; reporters will discard credentials they can't check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contact info and quick follow-up channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Give phone/email and indicate availability for follow-up; be reachable on short notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include 'Available for follow-up: [phone] / [email]' and a LinkedIn link if helpful. Reporters often need answers within hours, so note availability and respond promptly to follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include headshot link for byline needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer a headshot link in case the reporter needs an image for the byline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a direct link to a headshot (high-resolution if possible). This speeds publication and is requested frequently for online or print bylines.

rubrics_metrics.name: State willingness to be quoted by name
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate that you are willing to be quoted on the record by name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters favor sources who permit on-the-record quotes and who will stand behind the attribution; explicitly stating willingness can increase selection chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the sample pitch structure/order
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the recommended ordering: subject, greeting, ID/credentials, direct answer, examples/data, availability, headshot/links, signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample pitch template in the transcript prescribes: Subject line matching the query, 'Hi [Reporter]', immediate ID/credentials, a 2‑sentence direct answer, 1–2 supporting examples or data points, availability/contact, headshot link, LinkedIn, signature. Following this order makes your pitch scannable and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic answers and throat-clearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send generic responses that could come from anyone or long introductory paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid multi-paragraph 'throat-clearing' and broad platitudes. Specificity and immediacy are key; generic commentary is routinely ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pitch unrelated services or self-promote before answering
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't use the HARO response to promote unrelated services or lead with promotional language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters want expertise relevant to the query, not marketing copy. Answer the question first; excessive self-promotion or selling lowers the chance of being used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not ask for approval before quote use
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid asking reporters to get your approval before using a quote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asking for pre-approval or permission to review copy is a turn-off; reporters expect to use quotes as provided. If you need off-the-record status or review, negotiate that separately — but don't condition your quote's use in the initial HARO reply.
